# Pool 0.12.36
The agent library now includes every accessible document in Library, including books uploaded without a project. New uploads appear in the catalogue immediately and become searchable in full as server transcription completes.
Press-only documents stay outside the agent library. Full PDFs still download only when requested.

# Pool 0.12.35
Fixes startup for collaborators using private local Documents by including the local document library in the packaged macOS application.

# Pool 0.12.34
External collaborators can now use Documents without receiving access to the studio document archive. Their PDFs and Markdown files are kept in a private, searchable library on their own Mac and are never uploaded to Pool.
Local documents can be imported, searched, previewed, renamed and downloaded. The shared document controls are intentionally absent in this mode.

# Pool 0.12.33
Documents now includes **Connect agents**. Prepare a local Books library, copy the correct instruction for your own computer, and open its folder directly from Pool.
Codex and Claude Code can search available transcriptions and inspect selected PDF pages using Pool's bundled runtime. Each person uses their own Pool sign-in; catalogue and text stay lightweight, while original PDFs download only when requested.

Clean up the expanded image view so its essential actions remain visible and balanced. Search, source, privacy, creation, beacon, history, reflection, and team-note controls now use clearer compact groups without awkward wrapping or overlap. Reflection recording and saving remain distinct actions.
This update also preserves the current document workflow: PDFs up to 200 MB and UTF-8 Markdown files can be added to Documents, searched, previewed, and shared through the existing project permissions.

Fix carousel recordings getting stuck on Saving. A successful save now releases the controls immediately, even when refreshing the history is slow or unavailable. Saved reflections appear in the count directly from the save response.
Finishing transcription and saving now have distinct progress messages and bounded waits. If recognition or the connection stalls, the captured session stays in the open app with a working Retry save button. Retrying uses the same session identity to avoid duplicates. Recording and explicit sharing behavior are unchanged.

Record freely while moving through the image carousel. Click Record reflection once, use Previous and Next (or arrow keys) to move between images, then click Stop and save. Each passage stays attached to the image being viewed, including late recognition results and return visits. The microphone keeps running between images.
Stop and save commits all passages privately in one session. Failed saves retain the session for retry without duplicate reflections. Long sessions renew recognition without stopping capture, with a 30-minute recording limit. No audio file is stored.

Record reflections with a large button: click Record reflection, speak, then click Stop and save. Recording now uses Pool's authenticated local API, fixing the native bridge's incompatibility with the archive's script security policy. The existing policy remains strict and audio stays on the Mac without being saved. Live recognition replaces the previous hypothesis without duplicating phrases. Stop preserves the full live text if the recognizer returns a shorter final result. Completed utterances are retained across the on-device recognizer's pause resets, so a new phrase cannot replace speech recorded before a natural pause.
Choose a folder and click Reflect on folder for a guided image carousel with Previous, Next and a position count. This walks the full folder, including nested folders, independently of search filters. Each reflection stays attached to its image and private unless explicitly shared.

Pool now lets you speak or write a private reflection on an image, document or link. Open an image fullscreen for the reflection carousel, with Next, Previous and Random. Hold V to dictate on your Mac; release to save the transcript with the media identity and viewing/recording times. Audio is never saved, and native dictation requires on-device speech recognition.
Reflections stay separate from captions and team notes. They are private by default, synchronize through your account, and can be shared individually with people you explicitly trust. Trusting someone does not automatically share anything. Removing trust revokes their existing reflection grants.

Pool Documents now includes a Chrome clipper download and installation instructions in its sidebar. The clipper uses the current Pool logo and clearer save instructions.
Newly saved PDFs appear first in Documents, even when the original article was published earlier. Publication dates are preserved.
Download Pool-Capture-Chrome.zip from this release, unzip it, and load the Pool Capture folder through Chrome's Extensions page with Developer mode enabled. Existing users can replace their extension folder contents and click Reload.

# Pool 0.12.26
- Give Pool a new black-and-white app icon across the macOS app, archive interface, browser extension, and iOS source assets.

# Pool 0.12.25
- Send selected archive images, Projects, or Concepts directly into KILN and GRIDS. Both tools also support generation without references. - Save generated images with their native recipes, exact source snapshots, and source relationships. Browse saved generations, restore them, export recovery bundles, and retry pending uploads. - Create reusable CLIP beacons for images, Concepts, Projects, and stacks, with immutable versions, explicit refresh, and vector/manifest export. - Preserve archive permissions when restoring generated work and preserve the settings that produced KILN’s displayed image when saving.
Requires the generation-enabled archive server for shared inputs, results, and beacons. KILN and GRIDS currently accept image inputs; beacon-consuming generators and semantic canvases will follow separately.

# Pool 0.12.24
- Replace Press with Documents, keeping PDF ingestion, OCR, notes, folders, Concepts and original downloads. - Add administrator-configurable document types with optional text and date fields. Press coverage preserves existing publication, byline and dates; Library-only PDFs become Reference, with Library retained as a filter. - Edit document types and fields in the inspector, search custom metadata, and retain saved values when switching types.

# Pool 0.12.23
- Improve typed image searches by combining caption similarity with CLIP text-to-image matching, finding visual details that captions may omit. Queries are embedded locally using the existing image index. - Repair Google Lens searches after Google's URL-import flow became unreliable. Pool now submits a short-lived normalized JPEG as a file in the browser, while the high-resolution archive original remains private and unchanged.

# Pool 0.12.22
- Add a shared PDF Library beside Press, with multiple-file upload, full-text search, project and contributor filters, and original downloads. - Read PDFs in Pool and use the existing title/summary, team notes, project and concept controls. Library and Press share the Press archive permission. - Keep existing Press records unchanged. One PDF can appear in both collections without duplicating its file, notes or project assignments. - PDFs dropped into project folders now enter Library. Press capture imports continue to enter Press. - Fix embedded PDF previews and keep document rows stable during refresh.
Requires the updated team server. Library is a desktop feature; the native iOS client is unchanged.

# Pool 0.12.21
- Removes drag-to-select from the archive so dragging a thumbnail exports its full-resolution original. - Preserves checkbox and modifier-click selection for batch actions and exporting multiple images. - Prepares exports when hovering over any thumbnail, including unselected images.

# p∞l 0.12.4
- Requires one manual replacement install because Pool's updater signing key was reset; automatic updates resume after 0.12.4 is installed. - Restores the current Pool and embedded KILN interface, including the shared firing archive, restore controls, column mode, and batch generation. - Adds pinch-to-zoom and drag-to-pan to fullscreen image viewing, with zoom centered on the gesture and quick reset controls. - Preserves the full-resolution source switch and native image dragging when the fullscreen view is not zoomed. - Bundles the corrected KILN assets so future installs no longer fall back to the old standalone interface.
